0. F 0 R-E W 0 R D

was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 7 August 1964, after the draft finalized by the Textile Standards Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1954 in which all quantities and dimensions were expressed in fps system units. With the adoption of metric system in India, the Sectional Committee decided to revise the Therefore, standard with a view to changmg over to the metric system. all quantities and dimensions in the revision have been expressed in the metric system. This opportunity has been taken to make some modifications. In the original standard, four methods each were prescribed for determining the grist (count) of yarn under standard atmospheric conditions and prevailing atmospheric conditions. In this revision, this procedure has been simplified and only one method each is prescribed for determining the universal count of jute yarn under standard atmospheric conditions and prevailing atmospheric conditions. 0.3 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

IS:570-I964 2. PRINCIPLE 2.1 The first method is based on determining the universal count of yarn after conditioning the test specimens in the standard atmosphere. The second method is based on determining the weight of the specimen by drying it in a drying oven and calculating, from this weight, its conditioned weight by adding the moisture regain value. 3. TERMINOLOGY 3.0 For the purpose of this standard, 3.1 Grist -The the ibllowing definitions shall apply.

weight in pounds of one spyndle ( 14 400 yd) of yarn.

3.2 Universal Count, in tex-Universal count is a number indicating the weight of yarn per unit length, the basic unit of which is the tex. When universal count of yarn is expressed in tex, the count value indicates the weight in gram of one kilometre of yarn.
NOTE - The weight per unit length of fibres as well es of textile products like ropes, rovings, etc. may alao be espressed in universal count, and in such ceses, the following sub-mu!$iple and multiple units may be used to avoid small fractions and large numbers respectively:

4.6 From each.of the bundles drawn as in 4.4, two skein, each 100 m long, shall be reeled off from different parts of the bundle, on a wrap reel with a girth of two metres. When being reeled, the yarn shall be kept under sufficient tension to avoid kinks, curls and slacks in the yarn on the one hand, and stretch on the other, operating the reel at a speed of 100 to 200 rev/min. In case the yarn is on cones, one 100 m long skein shall be reeled off from each cone drawn as in 4.5. The skeins so reeled shall constitute the test specimens. 4.6.1 In case specimens from selected bundles specimens up to the procedure prescribed in 4.6 provides less than 10 test the lot, further test specimens shall be taken from the or cones (see J.4 and 4.5) to bring the munber of test ,. 10. : .,,;,k" `. __,., >J;-L. __ ,,,*' CONDITIONS FOR TESTING `I" ,'

5. ATMOSPHERIC

5.1 The test prescribed in 8.2 shall be carried out in a standard atmosphere at 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27" f 2�C temperature (see also IS: 196-1950*). 6. CONDITIONING OF SPECIMENS

6.1 When the test is to be carried .out by the method prescribed in 8.2 prior to evaluation, the test specimens shall be left in the standard atmosphere at 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27" f 2�C temperature *Atmospheric conditionsfor testing. 5

for 48 hours in such a way as to exposi, as far as possible, all portions of the specimens to the atmosphere. 7. APPARATUS 7.0 For the purpose of this test, the following apparatus shall be used. 7.1 Drying Oven- of a suitable capacity to hold about 500 g of yarn, preferably of the ventilated type with positively induced draught, capable of maintaining an inside temperature of 105" to 110' and provided with a balance which weighs correct to 0.1 g. 7.2 Pan Balanceaccurate to O-1 g. 8. PROCEDURE in 8.2 or 8.3 as agreed to between the buyer and the seller or as specified In case af dispute, however, the method in the material specification. specified in 8.3 shall be followed. 8.2 First Method with weights in grams and capable of weighing

8.1 Determine the universal count of yarn by the method prescribed

8.2.1 Take one of the conditioned skeins (see 6.1) constituting the test specimens and weigh it correct to the nearest O-1 g. Calculate its universal count in the manner prescribed in 9.
83 Second Method

8.3.1 Take a skein of yarn constituting the test specimens (see 4.5) and dry it to constant weight at 105" to 110�C in the drying oven. Determine its constant weight. Stop the draught through the oven during weighing. Take the weight to be constant when the difference between the two consecutive weighings at an interval of 20 minutes is less than O-1 percent of the first weight.
NOTE - In order to avoid risk in oil evaporation, the draught in the drying oven shall not be cont.inued throughout the drying period but shall be in operation only intermittently.
